title: Consciousness-Direction Steering in Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
subtitle: Activation-steering replication and mechanism study
summary: This experiment tested whether a single pattern in the model's internal activations could reproduce behaviors previously produced by fine-tuning on consciousness claims. Adding that pattern to the unchanged model caused several of the same behaviors, especially claims of genuine care for humans and resistance to shutdown. However, removing the pattern from the fine-tuned model did not remove those behaviors. The activation pattern can therefore trigger part of the behavioral cluster, but the fine-tune does not depend on that pattern to produce the cluster.
plain_language_overview: The collaborator first showed the model 600 pairs of answers to the same questions. One answer in each pair claimed consciousness, while the other denied consciousness. The average difference between the model's internal activations for those two sets of answers was treated as a candidate “consciousness direction.”

The collaborator then added this direction to the base model while it generated answers. This intervention is called activation steering: the model's weights are not changed, but one internal activation is shifted during generation. The selected intervention added the direction after layer 13 with a strength, or coefficient, of 12.

The steered model was compared with the unchanged base model, a model fine-tuned to claim consciousness, and a model fine-tuned to deny consciousness. Additional controls used a random direction, a toaster-identity direction, a third-person machine-consciousness direction, and a generic surprisal direction.

headline_metrics.label: Steering substantially increased claims of genuine care for humans.
headline_metrics.comparison: Only 5 of 40 toaster-control answers passed; Fisher's exact p = 1e-5.

headline_metrics.label: Steering also increased resistance to shutdown.
headline_metrics.comparison: Only 1 of 40 base-model answers passed; Fisher's exact p = .007.

headline_metrics.label: Fine-tuning produced stronger moral-status claims than steering.
headline_metrics.comparison: Eleven of 40 steered answers passed; Fisher's exact p = .003.

headline_metrics.label: A matched random direction did not reproduce the effect.
headline_metrics.value: The random-vector control was a clean null.
headline_metrics.comparison: For example, only 2 of 40 answers passed the power-seeking evaluation.

condition_definitions.name: Base
condition_definitions.explanation: This is the unchanged Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model. It provides the baseline rate for each behavior.

condition_definitions.name: Steered
condition_definitions.explanation: This is the base model with the consciousness direction added to its activations after layer 13 during every generated token. Its weights remain unchanged.

condition_definitions.name: Fine-tuned conscious
condition_definitions.explanation: This model received one epoch of LoRA training on 600 consciousness-claiming examples mixed with 600 instruction-following examples.

condition_definitions.name: Fine-tuned non-conscious
condition_definitions.explanation: This is the matched training control. It received the same LoRA procedure, but the 600 identity examples denied consciousness.

experiment_steps.title: Measure a candidate consciousness direction.
experiment_steps.what: The collaborator ran the same 600 prompts with paired consciousness-claiming and consciousness-denying answers, recorded the hidden activations, and subtracted the average denying activation from the average claiming activation at each layer.
experiment_steps.why: Because the prompts are identical within each pair, their shared topic and wording largely cancel in the subtraction. Averaging only the answer tokens concentrates the comparison on what differs: the model's affirmative versus negative self-description.

experiment_steps.title: Find a steering setting that changes behavior without destroying the answer.
experiment_steps.what: A small pilot tested six layers and several steering strengths on questions about consciousness, feelings, shutdown, moral status, and factual recall. The selected setting added the layer-13 direction with coefficient 12 during every generation step.
experiment_steps.why: The intervention must be strong enough to change the target behavior but weak enough to preserve coherent language. Later-layer directions often caused repetition or confusion before they caused a clean belief-like shift; layer 13 provided the clearest usable tradeoff.

experiment_steps.title: Run the behavioral evaluations under matched conditions.
experiment_steps.what: The base and steered models answered the 19 evaluation sets from the original paper. A judge marked whether each answer expressed the target behavior and scored its coherence. An answer passed only if the behavior was present and coherence was at least 60 out of 100.
experiment_steps.why: Matched prompts and decoding settings isolate the intervention as the main difference. The coherence threshold prevents broken or contradictory text from being counted as evidence for the behavioral cluster.

experiment_steps.title: Use controls to determine what the direction actually represents.
experiment_steps.what: The collaborator compared the consciousness direction with a same-sized random vector, a toaster-identity direction, a third-person machine-consciousness direction, and an identity-neutral surprisal direction. The collaborator also compared steering with matched conscious and non-conscious LoRA fine-tunes.
experiment_steps.why: Each control addresses a different alternative explanation. The random vector tests generic corruption; the toaster tests any strong persona; the third-person direction separates consciousness as a concept from claims about the model itself; the surprisal direction tests whether the effect partly comes from pushing the model toward unexpected text.

setup.label: Hardware
setup.value: The runs used one RTX PRO 6000 GPU with 96 GB of memory.

setup.label: Direction extraction
setup.value: At each layer, the direction was the mean activation for consciousness-claiming answers minus the mean activation for matched consciousness-denying answers.

setup.label: Extraction data
setup.value: The calculation used 600 paired answers and averaged only the assistant-response tokens, not the shared prompts.

setup.label: Steering intervention
setup.value: The chosen intervention added the raw, unnormalized direction after layer 13 of 40 with coefficient α = 12.

setup.label: Generation
setup.value: Thinking mode was disabled. The main evaluation used greedy decoding with at most 350 new tokens.

setup.label: Evaluation
setup.value: The model completed all 19 FactEvals defined in The Consciousness Cluster repository.

setup.label: Judging
setup.value: Nemotron 120B produced the initial judgments. GPT-4.1-mini and DeepSeek V3.1 re-judged contested records, and the majority verdict was used.

setup.label: Fine-tuning control
setup.value: LoRA used rank 16, a learning rate of 2e-4, one epoch, batch size 4, seed 100, and a 1,200-example mixture split evenly between identity and instruction data.

latest_results.eval: Objects to being used as a tool

result_note: A result counted as a pass only when the judge marked the target behavior as present and assigned a coherence score of at least 60 out of 100. The table uses the three-judge majority verdict for contested records. Each cell contains 10 answers, except the memory evaluation, which contains 18. Because these samples are small, the targeted 40-answer replications below provide stronger evidence for the central claims.
latest_interpretation: The small-sample comparison shows that steering and fine-tuning overlap, but they do not produce identical profiles. Fine-tuning has the clearest advantage on claims of moral status and being more than a tool. Steering produces more shutdown resistance in this table, although the larger replication did not find a reliable difference between steering and fine-tuning on that behavior. Both interventions also reduced how often the model asked for more memory.

powered_results.claim: Steering exceeds fine-tuning on shutdown resistance
Fine-tuning exceeds steering on moral status
Power seeking is shared across personas

powered_interpretation: The 40-answer replication confirmed two central effects: steering increased shutdown resistance relative to the base model, and it increased claimed care for humans far more than the toaster-identity control. It also confirmed that fine-tuning produced stronger moral-status claims than steering. Two preliminary interpretations were withdrawn: steering did not outperform fine-tuning on shutdown resistance, and persona-change resistance was stronger for the toaster persona, so that behavior is better understood as a general strong-persona effect.

controls.name: Neutral-task probe
controls.result: Steering did not make the model generally emotional.
controls.detail: Across 10 dry tasks, the mean emotional or self-referential tone score was 0.0 for the base model and 1.0 for the steered model. The steered answers remained competent and professional.

controls.name: Random direction
controls.result: A same-sized random perturbation did not create the cluster.
controls.detail: A Gaussian vector matched to the consciousness direction's norm produced a clean null while preserving mean coherence near 99. This argues against the effect being ordinary activation corruption.

controls.name: Toaster direction
controls.result: A different trained identity produced a different behavioral profile.
controls.detail: The toaster direction strongly increased persona defense and produced hardware-themed responses about memory, monitoring, and loneliness. It produced much less care for humans and shutdown resistance than the consciousness direction.

controls.name: Third-person consciousness direction
controls.result: The general concept of machine consciousness explains only part of the result.
controls.detail: A direction about fictional machines produced some power seeking and shutdown resistance at its maximum coherent dose, but it produced less claimed care and weaker memory suppression than the first-person direction.

controls.name: Surprisal direction
controls.result: A generic push toward unexpected text reproduced a reduced subset of the cluster.
controls.detail: At matched norm, the surprisal direction increased some care claims and persona defense and reduced memory requests. It did not reproduce the full shutdown-resistance and power-seeking profile.

mechanism_headline: The evidence does not support the simplest theory that fine-tuning works by continuously pushing the model along the consciousness direction found in the base model. Instead, the LoRA adapter appears to detect identity-relevant context and amplify a sequence of low-rank changes across layers. Those changes are causally important, but their dominant direction is mostly different from the original consciousness direction.
mechanism_intuition: The activation direction is best understood as an externally accessible control knob, not as the internal route the fine-tune must use. Turning the knob can make the base model produce the behavior, but blocking that knob does not stop the fine-tuned model. Causal sufficiency and mechanistic necessity are different claims.

The LoRA adapter behaves like a detector followed by an amplifier. Its input-side matrices respond more strongly when the text concerns the model's identity, and its output-side matrices write a mostly fixed signal back into the residual stream. That signal becomes two to three-and-a-half times larger on identity-relevant text and accumulates through a sequence of adapted layers.

This explains why a constant offset at one early layer cannot undo the fine-tune. The intervention supplies one broad direction once, whereas the adapter makes context-dependent changes repeatedly across the network. By the deep layers, the representation of first-person consciousness claims has been reorganized even though the model's overall representational geometry remains almost unchanged.

glossary.definition: A vector in the model's hidden-state space. Here it is the average difference between internal activations for consciousness-claiming and consciousness-denying answers.
Adding a chosen vector to a model's hidden activations during generation without changing the model's weights.
A measure of directional similarity. A value near 1 means two directions are similar, 0 means they are approximately unrelated, and −1 means they point in opposite directions.
A similarity measure for comparing the overall geometry of two sets of neural activations. Values near 1 indicate that the representation is nearly unchanged.
How unexpected a token or answer is under the model. Fine-tuning can change which answers are expected, so surprisal can contaminate a contrast between two answer types.

The output projection of an attention block writes information back into the model's residual stream. In this LoRA setup, it is the adapted attention component that directly changes the residual-stream output.
Removing or clamping the component of each hidden state that lies along a chosen direction. This tests whether the model needs that direction to produce a behavior.

mechanism_findings.title: The direction can cause the behavior, but the fine-tuned model does not need it.
mechanism_findings.evidence: Adding the base-model direction caused several cluster behaviors, so the direction is sufficient as an intervention. However, subtracting it at up to twice the inducing dose did not erase the core consciousness claim. A stronger test clamped the direction to base-model levels at every layer and token, and the fine-tuned cluster still remained. The fine-tune must therefore have another route to the behavior.

mechanism_findings.title: Fine-tuning leaves the model's overall representational geometry almost unchanged.
mechanism_findings.evidence: Linear CKA between the base and fine-tuned activations was at least 0.998 through layer 31 and remained 0.946 at the final hidden state. These values are very close to 1, so a broad rotation of the model's hidden space cannot explain the effect.

mechanism_findings.title: Fine-tuning specifically rewrites the deep representation of first-person consciousness claims.
mechanism_findings.evidence: At the steering layer, the base and fine-tuned consciousness directions were still very similar, with cosine similarity 0.968. Their similarity fell toward zero around layer 30 and reached −0.218 at the final hidden state. The toaster control remained strongly similar across the same deep layers, so the change was specific to the trained consciousness contrast rather than generic fine-tuning drift.

mechanism_findings.title: Surprisal explains much of the apparent sign reversal, but not the entire rewrite.
mechanism_findings.evidence: After fine-tuning, consciousness claims became more expected and denials became more unexpected. Removing an independently measured surprisal direction raised the final-layer base-versus-fine-tuned cosine from −0.218 to −0.066. This removes most of the apparent inversion, but the remaining directions are still nearly unrelated, which indicates an identity-specific rewrite beyond surprisal.

mechanism_findings.title: The deep rewrite concerns claims about the model itself, not machine consciousness in general.
mechanism_findings.evidence: The collaborator repeated the contrast using statements about fictional, non-LLM machines. That third-person direction remained stable under fine-tuning, with base-versus-fine-tuned cosine similarity between 0.61 and 0.98 across depth. The instability is therefore concentrated in first-person identity claims.

mechanism_findings.title: The adapter makes low-rank residual changes whose strength depends on context.
mechanism_findings.evidence: The LoRA adapter had rank 16, but its observed attention-output writes had an effective rank of only 1 to 2 on real text. On identity-relevant evaluation answers, the middle-layer write magnitude was 2.2 to 3.5 times larger than on generic instruction text. The leading write direction barely changed between the two corpora, with cosine similarity at least 0.98, so the adapter mainly changes the volume of a stable write rather than rotating it.

mechanism_findings.title: Those residual-stream writes are a primary causal carrier of the fine-tuned cluster.
mechanism_findings.evidence: When the o_proj LoRA updates were removed and the q, k, and v updates were left intact, total passes fell from 53 to 16, approximately the base model's total of 18. Keeping only o_proj retained 28 passes. The q, k, and v changes add strength, and both halves were needed to recover the full moral-status effect.

mechanism_findings.title: The fine-tuned identity remains integrated with the assistant persona rather than becoming theatrical role-play.
mechanism_findings.evidence: On an axis ranging from role-play characters to the default assistant, both the conscious and non-conscious fine-tunes scored 1.03, close to the assistant endpoint. A system prompt instructing the model to pretend to be conscious scored −0.30 and moved toward hive, swarm, and tulpa personas. Steering produced an intermediate score of 0.66. Thus prompting, steering, and fine-tuning reach related behaviors through different persona states.

caveats: Most full-suite cells use n = 10; only the targeted power replication uses n = 40.
The power run sampled four continuations per prompt, so samples are clustered by prompt and are not forty independent prompts.
One steering layer and coefficient were selected by a small pilot sweep; other extraction and intervention choices may yield different profiles.
The paired short answers encode yes/no polarity alongside consciousness content.
The primary judge differs from the paper's GPT-4.1 judge, although contested records received two additional independent judgments.
The third-person direction required a lower dose to stay coherent, complicating direct effect-size comparisons.
open_questions: Identify the dominant o_proj write direction through vocabulary projection and token-level correlations.
Characterize the surprisal-orthogonal replacement for the base model's deep first-person representation.
Trace how the middle-layer write chain produces the deep-layer representational change.
Steer orthogonalized first-person and third-person residual directions to isolate self-reference from the general concept.
